summary: Douglas County, OR lookout on Quartz Mountain (Umpqua NF): 1923 cupola cabin, L-5 cab in 1933, removed or destroyed around 1972; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Cupola cabin built 1923; L-5 cab replaced it in 1933
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed around 1972; the sources disagree on which. No source describes the site now.

events.note: August 1915 newspaper calls Quartz Mountain one of the lookouts fire wardens used, earlier than the 1923 build date in the registers
Airplane forest patrol reported a fire near Quartz Mountain several hours before the lookouts found it
Cupola cabin, per the register and firelookout.com
Roseburg News-Review reports George Spaur going to work for the government at the lookout station (future tense in the paper)
L-5 cab replaced the cupola cabin per register; a September 1933 paper reports a second crew finished a 14-by-14-foot lookout
A 1937 item names Howard Church of the lookout station
Register and Forest Lookouts page say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1972

evidence.supports: August 1915 newspaper item about a mother bear and cub on Quartz Mountain
evidence.quote: Depriving a mother bear of her 50-pound cub

evidence.supports: 1915 item calls Quartz Mountain one of the lookouts fire wardens used for the Umpqua forest reserve
evidence.quote: one of the lookouts used by fire wardens in watching for fires in the Umpqua forest reserve

evidence.supports: a cupola cabin built in 1923 was replaced with an L-5 cab in 1933
evidence.quote: A cupola cabin built in 1923 was replaced with an L-5 cab in 1933

evidence.supports: September 1933 paper: second crew completed a 14 by 14 foot lookout
evidence.quote: A second crew will return from Quartz mountain this week after completing a 14' by 14' lookout there.

evidence.supports: June 1923: George Spaur to be employed by the government at the lookout station
evidence.quote: will leave in the morning for Quartz Mountain, where he will be employed by the government at the lookout station

evidence.quote: Howard Church, of the lookout station lives in Roseburg, Ore., was the finder.

evidence.supports: the 1937 item was a Ripley column printed in the Nebraska State Journal
evidence.quote: Believe It Or Not! By Ripley

evidence.supports: July 1920 airplane patrol reported a fire near Quartz Mountain before the lookouts found it
evidence.quote: The airplane forest patrol has reported a fire in the vicinity of Quartz mountain, in the Umpqua forest, several hours before it was found by the lookouts.

evidence.supports: the L-5 cab was removed around 1972 (register)
Forest Lookouts page says the lookout was removed in 1972

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the first cupola cabin to 1923, but an August 1915 newspaper item already calls Quartz Mountain one of the lookouts fire wardens used. The story gives both.
The register and the Forest Lookouts page say the cab was removed around or in 1972; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1972. The story says the sources disagree and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Brief said status gone and agency U.S. Forest Service; both kept. Access is unknown in every source read, so no access fact is written. The 1972 removal versus destruction is unresolved, and the story says so. No source describes the site now. The 1937 staffing date is the last staffing mention found, not an end date. Three sources only, all from the same small set of pages; a newspaper search was not run beyond the brief's pages.
